chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from a number of our companions, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Abī al-Ḥārith, who said:
I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “May a man perform salat (prayer) in a garment of silk?” He said: “No.”

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: a man; the subject of the legal ruling
key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Riḍā, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.ثَوْبِ: a garment or piece of clothing

ai.seo_question: Can a man perform salat (prayer) in a silk garment according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a direct legal ruling from Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام regarding salat (prayer) in a silk garment. It indicates that a man may not perform salat (prayer) while wearing a garment made of silk.
